sections.heading: Why Door Closer Repairs Cannot Wait
sections.body: A malfunctioning door closer is more than a minor inconvenience. When a closer loses hydraulic pressure, develops a broken arm, or begins slamming doors uncontrollably, it puts tenants, customers, and employees at risk of injury. Doors that fail to latch properly can also compromise building security and climate control, allowing conditioned air to escape and unauthorized access to become easier. In a dense commercial environment like Washington DC, where buildings see hundreds or thousands of daily foot traffic events, even a single faulty closer can accelerate wear on the door frame, hinges, and hardware. Addressing the problem promptly prevents what might be a straightforward repair from becoming a costly full-door replacement. Our technicians carry commonly needed parts on their service vehicles so many repairs are completed in a single visit, reducing disruption to your building operations and keeping your tenants satisfied.

sections.heading: Signs Your Commercial Door Closer Needs Attention
sections.body: Catching door closer problems early saves money and prevents more serious damage. Common warning signs include a door that slams shut instead of closing gently, a door that swings open too forcefully when pushed, a closer arm that visibly droops or wobbles, oil staining on or around the closer body indicating hydraulic fluid leakage, or a door that no longer latches reliably after closing. Squealing, grinding, or popping sounds during door operation often signal worn internal components or inadequate lubrication. If occupants are propping doors open to avoid dealing with a problem closer, that is a clear indicator that service is overdue. Regular inspection of door closers as part of a building maintenance routine helps identify these issues before they escalate. We are happy to assess multiple units during a single service visit, making it easy for property managers to address several problem closers at once.
